decisions.reason: As a very recent launch with a stated 2019 release timing and some market access limits, it remains an uncertain but still open option whose likely low holding cost argues for keeping it another year.
This small volume ionization chamber fits the firm's core dosimetry portfolio, and after only about a year there is too little evidence of failure to justify abandoning the option.
Because it is another core-technology chamber variant, management would likely keep it on the market while demand and product-market fit are still being learned at relatively low incremental cost.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is close to established customer needs and the firm's capabilities, so the option value of staying in the market is high and near-term withdrawal is unlikely.
This relative dosimetry chamber appears to be a targeted extension of the core line, and with limited time since launch the firm would usually keep it unless clear negative evidence emerged.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional adjacent product for such a manufacturer, making continued market presence the more likely choice while uncertainty resolves.
